label: Flagship proof · 3 minutes
title: The payment succeeded. The app said it failed.

scenes.title: The payment succeeded.
scenes.body: The process crashed before the application learned the truth.
scenes.voice: The payment was broadcast successfully. Then the process lost certainty before the application learned the truth. This is where ordinary payment glue becomes dangerous.

scenes.title: The application marked it failed.
scenes.body: But broadcast already crossed the point of no return.
scenes.voice: The naive state machine marks the operation failed. But after broadcast, failed is not a fact. It is an unsafe guess.

scenes.title: Read → pay → record
scenes.body: A crash between those steps can release value twice.
scenes.voice: If budget is read, then payment happens, then the result is recorded, a crash between those steps can release value twice.

scenes.title: Agent payments fail on glue, not validators.
scenes.body: Correctness is end-to-end state convergence.
scenes.voice: The hard problem is not another validator. It is keeping one truthful state across policy, signing, providers, chain execution, and reconciliation.

scenes.kicker: THE AUDIT FOUND FOUR FAILURE MODES
scenes.title: Mutable allow · Budget TOCTOU · Post-broadcast lie · FIFO reconcile
scenes.voice: The audit exposed four failures: mutable allow limits, budget time-of-check time-of-use, false certainty after broadcast, and FIFO reconciliation.

scenes.title: Every boundary must preserve identity and truth.
scenes.body: Intent → Policy → Session → Signature → Hook → Receipt → Reconcile
scenes.voice: Railguard organizes the correction around one invariant. Intent becomes policy, session, signature, execution, receipt, and reconciliation without changing identity.

scenes.title: Reserve before execution.
scenes.body: Commit only after settlement fact. Release only before broadcast.
scenes.voice: Budget authorization becomes atomic. Reserve before execution. Commit after settlement fact. Release only while broadcast has definitely not happened.

scenes.title: Unknown is a real safety state.
scenes.body: It freezes retry until reconciliation establishes truth.
scenes.voice: Unknown is not an error message. It is a safety state. It freezes retry while the reconciler establishes whether value actually moved.

scenes.title: Reconcile by executionDigest.
scenes.body: Never let queue order decide which payment a receipt belongs to.
scenes.voice: Receipts reconcile by execution digest, not by whichever reservation happens to be oldest. Queue order is not payment identity.

scenes.title: Tests, receipts, and public evidence.
scenes.body: Base Sepolia · Stellar testnet · APF-003/004 · CDP flow
scenes.voice: The repository exposes adversarial tests, receipt schemas, Base Sepolia and Stellar testnet evidence, and end-to-end CDP flow evidence.

scenes.title: What v0.1 does not claim.
scenes.voice: This is a reference implementation, not a mainnet product. HSM or MPC signing, deep reorg rewind, and full production operations remain open.

scenes.title: Make the failure reproducible.
scenes.body: Run the demo · inspect the evidence · challenge the state machine
scenes.voice: Do not trust the claim. Reproduce the failure, inspect the evidence, and challenge the state machine.

scenes.title: Reproduce four payment failures.
scenes.body: Then inspect exactly where the fixes live.
scenes.voice: This walkthrough reproduces four payment correctness failures, shows where each fix lives, and ends with the evidence and honest limitations of the reference release.

scenes.title: Pre-sign · Execute · Reconcile
scenes.voice: The system spans three boundaries: pre-sign x402 policy, SignGate and on-chain enforcement, then CDP execution and reconciliation.

scenes.title: One reviewer path.
scenes.voice: Start with make test, read the fixed failure-mode table, then run the canonical end-to-end script. Those three steps connect claims to executable proof.

scenes.title: Limits belong inside the intent hash.
scenes.body: A signature must bind the payment ceilings it authorizes.
scenes.voice: First, mutable allow. If limits sit outside the signed intent, policy can approve one thing while execution receives another. Railguard binds ceilings into the intent hash.

scenes.title: Authorization is a state transition.
scenes.body: Reserve atomically before money can move.
scenes.voice: Second, budget time-of-check time-of-use. A balance read followed by payment is not authorization. The budget must be reserved atomically before execution.

scenes.title: One allow. Three blocks.
scenes.voice: The contract demo shows one allowed path and three blocked attacks. The important point is that the on-chain ceiling remains independent of application optimism.

scenes.title: After broadcast: unknown, not failed.
scenes.body: Unknown freezes retry until settlement truth is recovered.
scenes.voice: Third, post-broadcast failure. Once a transaction may have escaped, failed is unsafe. Railguard records unknown and prevents retry until reconciliation recovers truth.

scenes.title: Unknown survives retries.
scenes.body: Submitted and unknown rows remain protected from accidental release.
scenes.voice: The payment-state tests verify that ambiguous outcomes become unknown, submitted or unknown rows block retry, and repeated execution is idempotent.

scenes.title: Oldest is not identity.
scenes.body: Receipts must select the exact submitted execution.
scenes.voice: Fourth, FIFO reconciliation. The oldest reservation is not necessarily the payment represented by a receipt. Ordering cannot substitute for identity.

scenes.title: executionDigest binds the flow.
scenes.body: Intent → execution → receipt → reconciliation
scenes.voice: An execution digest binds intent, submitted execution, receipt, and reconciliation so the exact payment is updated instead of a convenient queue entry.

scenes.title: Application state is not settlement fact.
scenes.voice: Each layer owns different facts. The application owns intent, the provider owns submission information, the chain owns settlement, and the reconciler makes them converge.

scenes.title: Inspect, do not infer.
scenes.body: evidence/ · receipts · transaction hashes · test outputs
scenes.voice: The evidence directory contains network-specific records, receipts, transaction identifiers, and test outputs. The release asks reviewers to inspect rather than infer.

scenes.title: Reference implementation ≠ production system.
scenes.voice: Known work remains: Postgres boundary fault injection, deep reorg rewind, HSM or MPC cosigners, and dependency audit cleanup. No mainnet funds are in scope.

scenes.title: Can another repository keep the check in CI?
scenes.voice: The real adoption test is simple. Another repository should run one profile, get one report, and open one useful issue without contacting the author.

scenes.title: Run it. Break it. Improve the profile.
scenes.body: github.com/prasanthkuna/railguard-new/blob/master/docs/PORTFOLIO.md
scenes.voice: Railguard version zero point one is a reference release. Run it, break it, inspect the proof, and help improve the failure profile.
